recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + Audit foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums in shared-types are consumed by every other module. Audit module is required by GP-002 for all state-changing operations. Both have no internal dependencies.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Leave Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types and audit. Defines the policy rules (max days per leave type per fiscal year) that balance and request modules consume. Must exist before balance initialization or request validation can work.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-types, leave-policy, and audit. Tracks per-employee balances per leave type per fiscal year. Required by leave-request for validation and deduction/restore operations.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Leaf module with no internal dependencies. Can be built in parallel with Phase 3. Required by leave-request for notifying employees and managers on submission/decision events.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Leave Request module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior modules. Orchestrates the full leave request lifecycle: validates against policy, checks/deducts/restores balances, audits every state change, and triggers notifications. This is the integration point.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes), application (services), domain (models + repository interfaces), infrastructure (repository implementations + db). Dependencies flow inward: routes → services → repositories → db. All modules export only through index.ts barrel. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums are pure value types used by multiple modules → placed in src/shared/types/. Every state-changing service method (submit, approve, reject, cancel, upsertPolicy, deductBalance, restoreBalance, initializeBalances) must call IAuditService.recordEvent per GP-002. LeaveRequestService is the orchestrator: on submitRequest it validates against ILeavePolicyService, checks balance via ILeaveBalanceService, persists via ILeaveRequestRepository, and notifies via INotificationService. On approveRequest it deducts balance; on rejectRequest or cancelRequest (if previously approved) it restores balance. All balance mutations are transactional within the service method.

open_questions.question: How does leave balance accrual work — annual lump-sum allocation at fiscal-year start vs. monthly pro-rata accrual?
open_questions.impact: Determines the data model for LeaveBalance (carry-over rules, accrual schedule), the initializeBalances implementation, and whether a background job scheduler is needed.
candidate_options: Annual lump-sum: full entitlement granted on fiscal-year start date
Monthly pro-rata: entitlement accrues monthly (e.g., annual/12 per month)
Hybrid: lump-sum for annual/sick, pro-rata for emergency

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal year boundary — calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) or a configurable company fiscal year?
open_questions.impact: Affects every balance query, policy lookup, and the fiscalYear parameter semantics across all service methods.
candidate_options: Configurable per-tenant fiscal year (e.g., Apr 1 – Mar 31)

open_questions.question: When a leave request is approved, should the balance be deducted immediately at approval time or at the start of the leave period?
open_questions.impact: Binding computation semantics — affects deductBalance call timing in approveRequest and the restoreBalance behavior on cancellation. Must be consistent across all balance-affecting operations.
candidate_options: Deduct on the first day of the leave period

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole }; UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'; JWT bearer verified by auth middleware that populates request.user; RBAC enforced by requireRole(...) route-level guard, never inline. leave-policy routes: upsertPolicy requires hr_admin; getPolicyForType/getAllPolicies require authenticated user. leave-balance routes: getBalance/getAllBalances require employee (own) or manager (team). leave-request routes: submitRequest/cancelRequest require employee; approveRequest/rejectRequest require manager; getPendingRequestsForManager requires manager.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code: VALIDATION_ERROR). Authentication failure → 401 (code: UNAUTHORIZED). Authorization failure → 403 (code: FORBIDDEN). Not found → 404 (code: NOT_FOUND). Insufficient balance → 400 (code: INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE). Policy violation (e.g., exceeds max days) → 400 (code: POLICY_VIOLATION). Invalid state transition (e.g., approving an already-rejected request) → 409 (code: INVALID_STATE).
